# Jujube Fruit

13(4): 607-611</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahman E, Momin A, Zhao L, Guo X, Xu D, Zhou F, Ji B · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Bioactive, nutritional composition, heavy metal and pesticide residue of four Chinese jujube cultivars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Biotechnology (2018) 27(2):323-331</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nie JY, Kuang LX, Li ZX, Xu WH, Wang C, Chen QS, Li A, Zhao XB, Xie HZ, Zhao DY, Wu YL, Cheng Y · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals">Assessing the concentration and potential health risk of heavy metals in China&#39;s main deciduous fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Integrative Agriculture 2016, 15(7): 1645-1655</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Across 2 other studies of ordinary farms and markets, reported lead means and medians on a dry-weight basis ranged from 4.16 µg/kg (Du et al. 2025) to 4,200 µg/kg (Yan et al. 2014).<sup class="cite">[[sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Du X, Guo SG, Wang WJ · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements">Analysis of heavy element content in Shanxi specialty Ziziphus jujuba Mill. and health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Safety &amp; Quality 2025, 16(8): 100-106 (in Chinese with English abstract)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yan Q, Liu Y, Yang L · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Analysis of Essential and Toxic Elements in Jujube Fruits Collected from Different Locations in China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Tropical Journal of Pharmaceutical Research April 2014; 13(4): 607-611</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Rahman et al. 2018 reported cadmium at 13.9 µg/kg (mean), total arsenic at 26.1 µg/kg (mean) and total mercury at 2.44 µg/kg (mean) in jujube Fruit, as sold from cv. Hupingzao (HPZ), Minqin county, Gansu, China.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahman E, Momin A, Zhao L, Guo X, Xu D, Zhou F, Ji B · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Bioactive, nutritional composition, heavy metal and pesticide residue of four Chinese jujube cultivars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Biotechnology (2018) 27(2):323-331</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the jujube Fruit came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-jujube-fruit" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-jujube-fruit-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of jujube fruit, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

id="hmi-occurrence-jujube-fruit-methods" data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:jujube-fruit-b738bfc35e67:01f36c6452ba"><summary>HMI jujube fruit Pb reference · Jujube Fruit, dried, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:jujube-fruit-b738bfc35e67:01f36c6452ba"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI jujube fruit Pb reference · Jujube Fruit, dried, dry weight. Jujube Fruit, dried; Dry weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>4.16</td><td>16.6</td><td>29</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>4.16</td><td>16.6</td><td>29</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>2 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Du et al. 2025</td><td>2</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for jujube fruit, dried on a dry weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Du et al. 2025 is the only compatible sampling family for jujube fruit, dried on this basis in the completed jujube fruit ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Du et al. 2025</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:jujube-fruit-b738bfc35e67:01f36c6452ba</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:jujube-fruit-9b40d0651423:25dcf5933a21"><summary>HMI jujube fruit Cd reference · Jujube Fruit, dried, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:jujube-fruit-9b40d0651423:25dcf5933a21"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI jujube fruit Cd reference · Jujube Fruit, dried, dry weight. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach jujube Fruit

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

No study in the library compared jujube Fruit from contaminated and ordinary settings, so the routes by which metals reach it are not measured here.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

In one study, lead across 4 groups of jujube Fruit ranged from 3,000 µg/kg (commercial dried jujube, Hebei origin) to 4,200 µg/kg (commercial dried jujube, Xinzheng (Henan) origin); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yan Q, Liu Y, Yang L · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Analysis of Essential and Toxic Elements in Jujube Fruits Collected from Different Locations in China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Tropical Journal of Pharmaceutical Research April 2014; 13(4): 607-611</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, total arsenic across 4 groups of jujube Fruit ranged from 10.3 µg/kg (cv. Hupingzao (HPZ), Minqin county, Gansu, China) to 100 µg/kg (cv. Xiaozao (XZ), Minqin county, Gansu, China); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahman E, Momin A, Zhao L, Guo X, Xu D, Zhou F, Ji B · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Bioactive, nutritional composition, heavy metal and pesticide residue of four Chinese jujube cultivars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Biotechnology (2018) 27(2):323-331</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Reporting limits for lead ranged from 4 µg/kg (Du et al. 2025) to 5 µg/kg (Nie et al. 2016), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Du X, Guo SG, Wang WJ · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements">Analysis of heavy element content in Shanxi specialty Ziziphus jujuba Mill. and health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Safety &amp; <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Jujube Fruit FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-jujube-fruit" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-jujube-fruit" data-question="What heavy metals are found in jujube Fruit?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in jujube Fruit?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, Cu, Fe, Mn, Ca and Mg in jujube Fruit, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Du X, Guo SG, Wang WJ · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements">Analysis of heavy element content in Shanxi specialty Ziziphus jujuba Mill. and health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Safety &amp; Quality 2025, 16(8): 100-106 (in Chinese with English abstract)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/du2025-shanxi-jujube-heavy-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yan Q, Liu Y, Yang L · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Analysis of Essential and Toxic Elements in Jujube Fruits Collected from Different Locations in China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Tropical Journal of Pharmaceutical Research April 2014; 13(4): 607-611</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahman E, Momin A, Zhao L, Guo X, Xu D, Zhou F, Ji B · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Bioactive, nutritional composition, heavy metal and pesticide residue of four Chinese jujube cultivars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Biotechnology (2018) 27(2):323-331</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Nie JY, Kuang LX, Li ZX, Xu WH, Wang C, Chen QS, Li A, Zhao XB, Xie HZ, Zhao DY, Wu YL, Cheng Y · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals">Assessing the concentration and potential health risk of heavy metals in China&#39;s main deciduous fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Integrative Agriculture 2016, 15(7): 1645-1655</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/nie2016-china-deciduous-fruits-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-jujube-fruit-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-jujube-fruit-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of jujube Fruit measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of jujube Fruit measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 4 groups of jujube Fruit ranged from 3,000 µg/kg (commercial dried jujube, Hebei origin) to 4,200 µg/kg (commercial dried jujube, Xinzheng (Henan) origin); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Yan Q, Liu Y, Yang L · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Analysis of Essential and Toxic Elements in Jujube Fruits Collected from Different Locations in China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Tropical Journal of Pharmaceutical Research April 2014; 13(4): 607-611</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/yan2014-china-jujube-essential-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, total arsenic across 4 groups of jujube Fruit ranged from 10.3 µg/kg (cv. Hupingzao (HPZ), Minqin county, Gansu, China) to 100 µg/kg (cv. Xiaozao (XZ), Minqin county, Gansu, China); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rahman E, Momin A, Zhao L, Guo X, Xu D, Zhou F, Ji B · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Bioactive, nutritional composition, heavy metal and pesticide residue of four Chinese jujube cultivars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Biotechnology (2018) 27(2):323-331</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rahman2018-chinese-jujube-cultivars-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
